best_for: Writers, journalists and privacy-minded professionals who want encrypted notes synced across all their devices for free, and who may pay later for richer editors and file storage.
description:
Standard Notes is an encrypted notes app from Standard Notes, an independent company that says it has taken no venture capital and lives entirely on what paying users spend. It has been running for 10 years, and its code is open and checked by outside security researchers.

People keep far more than notes in it: budgets, to-do lists, code snippets, passwords and keys, journals, health records and photos of passports or IDs. An offline copy stays on your device, so your notes open without an internet connection. You can also publish posts through Listed, the company's blogging platform.

points.title: Sync on every device is free
points.text: The free Standard plan includes end-to-end encryption, sync across unlimited devices, plain text notes, tags, two-factor sign-in and daily encrypted backups by email. The catch: note history on the free plan covers only the current session.

points.title: Rich notes are the paid line
points.text: The Super note type (markdown, rich text, checklists), spreadsheets, folders, the web clipper and one year of revision history start at Productivity, listed at USD 90 per year. Professional is USD 120 per year and adds 100 GB of encrypted file storage and sharing the plan with up to 5 accounts. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: What happens when a plan lapses
points.text: Paid features stop right away. Notes written in paid editors turn view-only until you switch them to plain text, and uploaded files can no longer be opened or downloaded, so save copies before you cancel.

points.title: You can skip the account
points.text: The help center says the app works fully offline with no account. Notes then stay on that one device, and you set an application passcode to keep them encrypted.

points.title: Run your own server
points.text: The desktop app has a built-in Home Server that serves devices on your local network while the app is open. You can also self-host the server with Docker. The code is open source under AGPL-3.0.

points.title: Windows keeps the long history
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 590 versions, with 32-bit and 64-bit installers. macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon zips) and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is not marked verified
points.text: The Flathub build names Standard Notes Ltd. as developer, but Flathub does not mark it as verified. It runs on x64 and ARM64 and is about 160 MB to download.
